title: Singapore's Study into Feasibility of Nuclear Energy to Meet our Energy Needs
what_it_is: Singapore's Study into Feasibility of Nuclear Energy to Meet our Energy Needs

sections.label: New nuclear reactor designs
sections.summary: The study found conventional large reactors unsuitable for Singapore, but new designs like Small Modular Reactors and Generation IV may be much safer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The study found that conventional large reactor technologies were not suitable for deployment in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: However, since then, new designs are in the process of being developed that have the potential to be much safer than many of the plants in operation today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: These include Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) and "Generation IV" nuclear technologies, which incorporate enhanced safety systems that may not be possible for old generation technologies.

sections.label: Advanced energy technologies in development
sections.summary: Nuclear fusion could theoretically produce clean electricity, but advanced geothermal and nuclear technologies remain in research and development without commercial operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Hence, nuclear fusion power plants can, at least theoretically, produce clean electricity to meet our energy needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: However, many of these advanced geothermal and nuclear technologies are still in the research and development phase, and have not begun commercial operations yet.

sections.label: Singapore's nuclear technology assessment
sections.summary: The 2012 pre-feasibility study concluded conventional fission technologies are unsuitable for Singapore, but new technologies like nuclear fusion could be much safer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Government concluded in the pre-feasibility study in 2012 that conventional nuclear technologies primarily using fission technology, such as those deployed in Fukushima and the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plants, are not suitable for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: However, as I mentioned earlier, there are new kinds of nuclear technology, like nuclear fusion technology, that are being developed globally that will have the potential to be much safer than the older designs that the Member had raised earlier.

sections.label: No energy mix target set
sections.summary: The Government has not set any energy mix target, and most technology remains in research and development, not yet commercially deployed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Government has not yet set any target for the energy mix in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On why we need to wait until 2050 and whether we can deploy this sooner, as I mentioned earlier, most of the technology is currently in the research and development phase and has not yet been commercially deployed.
